To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the higher-order statistics of primordial perturbations are powerful tools to infer the inflation model, that the non-Gaussianities can be inferred from the observed perturbative spectra and the primordial spectra can be reconstructed from the observed ones.

the higher-order statistics of inflationary models can be used to discriminate among them and that this method can be applied to observational data, that non-Gaussianity is an important tool to measure the primordial power spectra and that this is possible for the first time in the case of a partial sky coverage.

the higher-order statistics of primordial curvature perturbations allow to discriminate between viable inflation models and that the primordial power spectra of curvature perturbation and tensor perturbation can be inferred from observations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the inference of inflation models from observational cosmological data.
a generic approach to infer inflation models from observational constraints on the curvature perturbation and its non-Gaussianity.
the reconstruction of primordial power spectra from cosmological observations and the discrimination of inflation models based on their higher-order statistics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the higher-order statistics approach is the method of choice for generic inference of inflation models and the critical filter and smoothness prior approaches are the methods of choice for primordial power spectrum reconstructions.
the higher-order statistics of primordial perturbations and their power spectra are the most promising observables to distinguish among viable inflation models.

the higher-order statistics of curvature perturbations and its primordial power spectrum allow to discriminate among inflation models and to infer the non-Gaussianity of the observed perturbation, which is a key ingredient for the determination of the primordial power spectra.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the higher-order statistics approach allows for the inference of inflationary models, while the power spectrum reconstruction enables to measure the primordial power spectra and non-Gaussianity.

it is a first step towards a generic inference method of the primordial power spectra and higher order statistics of curvature perturbation from observations, with a focus on the non-Gaussianity of primordial perturbations.
we have presented a generic method for inflation model inference from observational data by higher-order statistics and have shown that it is applicable to the still viable inflationary models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the primordial power spectra can be reconstructed from observations and that higher-order statistics are a promising tool for generic inference of inflation models.
the combination of the higher-order statistical methods and the power spectrum reconstruction is a promising way to constrain inflation models.
a combination of the methods presented in this work will allow to infer inflationary models from observational data.
